examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
examples.problem: Express $\cos\left( x - \dfrac{\pi}{2} \right)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(u - v) = \cos u \cos v + \sin u \sin v
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $u = x$ and $v = \dfrac{\pi}{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot 0+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $u=x$ and $v={315}^{∘}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{315}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{315}^{∘}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{315}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
